about: Advisories the weekly watch doesn't raise, each with why. npm entries are by package and cover only packages outside the web vault and the extension; cargo entries are by advisory and package version. Review the reasons whenever what we ship changes.

npm.node-forge: Only the command-line client (apps/cli) uses it, and we don't ship the CLI yet. Revisit before we do.
npm.multer: Only the command-line client's local server (bw serve) uses it, and we don't ship the CLI yet. Revisit before we do.
npm.inquirer: Only the command-line client's prompts use it, and we don't ship the CLI yet. Revisit before we do.
npm.external-editor: Comes with inquirer, in the command-line client only.
npm.tmp: Comes with inquirer, in the command-line client only.
npm.ws: Node's WebSocket, under SignalR. The browser apps use the browser's own WebSocket; only the command-line client would load it.
npm.vite: Build tooling (through vite-tsconfig-paths); none of it runs in the web vault or the extension.
npm.immutable: Comes with vite, build tooling only.
npm.nanoid: Comes with vite and postcss, build tooling only.
npm.picomatch: Comes with vite, build tooling only.
npm.postcss: Comes with vite, build tooling only: it reads only our own CSS.
npm.source-map-js: Comes with postcss, build tooling only.

cargo.RUSTSEC-2023-0071 rsa 0.9.10: No fixed version exists. The server signs its login tokens with it (jsonwebtoken, also openidconnect), as upstream Vaultwarden does; the timing leak needs very many precisely timed private-key operations. The desktop agent only encrypts with a public key, which the attack doesn't affect. Revisit when rsa has a fix, or move jsonwebtoken to its aws-lc-rs backend.
cargo.RUSTSEC-2026-0349 rustls 0.21.12: From Rocket 0.5.1, for serving TLS itself; this advisory is about TLS clients or features Rocket doesn't use, and our deployments terminate TLS at a reverse proxy. Revisit when Rocket moves to a newer rustls.
